key_insight: Bayesian inverse modeling generates virtual aortic patient cohorts whose geometries are compatible with prescribed hemodynamic biomarkers.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports uncertainty-aware cardiovascular simulation by identifying multiple plausible anatomies consistent with a target pressure drop.
method: Encode vascular shape in a high-dimensional latent space using a conditional LDDMM stochastic interpolant.
Evaluate biomarkers with an unsteady incompressible Navier–Stokes finite element solver.
Compare EAKI, aBUS, and WFR sequential Monte Carlo, introducing a differentiable flow-matching surrogate for WFR.
evidence_signal: The three methods are validated and compared on synthetic data for aortic coarctation cohorts matching prescribed pressure drops.
watch_item: The surrogate reduces forward-evaluation cost but introduces distribution shift that depends on its training distribution.
paper_title: Inverse domain uncertainty quantification in hemodynamics: sampling virtual patient cohorts under constraints
